name: ambilight-holds-through-a-cold-open
description:
Round 2: opening a cold tab must not flash the space default between the old tab's glow and the new page's first read. The commit arrives with no theme-color and no favicon yet, and the event path used to answer that with the plain space tint - one jump to the default, then a second jump when the sampler read the new page. While the sampler is live the event path holds the glow instead.

The control is the commit of the cold page; the measurement is the hold line on that commit and the ABSENCE of a uniform tint being pushed between the two pages' glows.

actions.note: the split page commits and the sampler starts on it

actions.expression: (() => { const rows = document.querySelector('.railpane:not(.ovrailpane)').querySelectorAll('[data-dropzone="tabs"] .tabrow'); if (rows.length < 2) { return 'rows ' + rows.length; } const b = rows[1].getBoundingClientRect(); return '100,' + Math.round((b.top + b.bottom) / 2 + 30); })()
actions.note: the second row's centre on screen, 30px below its client y, so a layout change cannot move the click off it
the Brand row, COLD - it navigates, which is the case under test
the cold tab's page, read from the page itself

assertions.label: the-cold-page-committed
assertions.desc: THE CONTROL: the cold tab navigated, so the event path had a colourless commit to answer.

assertions.pattern: Atrium: page tint held for the sampler
assertions.label: the-glow-held
assertions.desc: THE MEASUREMENT: the colourless commit was answered with a hold, not with the space default.

assertions.label: the-new-page-then-glowed
assertions.desc: And the sampler's own read of the new page arrived after the hold, so the chrome went from the split page's glow straight to this one.
